questions.q: What was the primary goal of the Indian freedom struggle that deeply influenced the framing of the Constitution regarding people's participation in governance?
questions.a: The primary goal was self-governance and democracy, which influenced the Constitution to establish a system where citizens elect their representatives through universal adult suffrage. A wrong answer shows a misunderstanding of the freedom movement as a mere change of rulers rather than a revolution for people's sovereignty.

questions.q: Why did freedom fighters place so much emphasis on equality before the law long before independence?
questions.a: Under British rule, laws favored the colonizers and discriminated against Indians, leading freedom fighters to demand absolute equality. A wrong answer reveals a belief that equality was a British gift rather than a hard-won democratic right fought for by Indian nationalists.

questions.q: During the freedom struggle, leaders like Motilal Nehru (1928) and the Karachi Session (1931) demanded fundamental rights for all Indians. How did this impact the drafting of the Constitution?
questions.a: These historic resolutions served as blueprints for the Constituent Assembly, ensuring that fundamental rights like freedom of speech and equality were given top priority in Part III of the Constitution. A wrong answer suggests the Constitution's rights were invented overnight without any historical roots.

questions.q: Analyze how the struggle against British censorship and press control shaped the constitutional provisions regarding media and expression.
questions.a: The British frequently banned newspapers and jailed journalists who criticized the government. To prevent this tyranny, the framers included the Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression under Article 19, ensuring a free press in democratic India. A wrong answer indicates confusion between colonial censorship and democratic accountability.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "The Indian Constitution is merely a copy of British legal systems, ignoring the Indian freedom struggle." Is this accurate?
questions.a: This statement is false because while procedural aspects borrowed British parliamentary forms, the core values—such as secularism, universal adult franchise, and social justice—were born directly out of the anti-colonial freedom struggle. A wrong answer shows failure to distinguish between administrative machinery and foundational national values.

questions.q: Design a short resolution for a hypothetical freedom movement that demands protection for marginalized workers, and explain how it would translate into a constitutional provision today.
questions.a: A good response would draft a demand for fair wages and no forced labor (echoing the Karachi Resolution) and link it directly to the Right against Exploitation in the Constitution. A poor answer focuses only on general complaints without proposing concrete legal rights.
